Purpose: Adds the specified Active Directory domain user to this computer's local Administrators group.
How to run: Replace DOMAIN and user with the intended account, then paste this file into Command Prompt opened as administrator.

Purpose: Adds the specified Entra ID user to this computer's local Administrators group.
How to run: Replace user@example.com with the intended sign-in UPN, then paste this file into Command Prompt opened as administrator on the Entra-joined device.

Purpose: Shows whether the local account named Administrator is enabled and includes an optional command to disable it.
How to run: Paste this file into elevated 64-bit PowerShell and uncomment the disable command only when that change is intended.

Purpose: Shows this device's Entra ID and domain join status along with user registration and SSO details.
How to run: Open Command Prompt as the affected signed-in user and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Displays the current account, SID, group memberships, and privileges in its security token.
How to run: Open Command Prompt in the affected user's normal session and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Lists user accounts in the computer's Active Directory domain rather than accounts stored only on this machine.
How to run: Open Command Prompt on a domain-joined computer with domain connectivity and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Lists every member of the local Administrators group, including local, domain, and Entra ID entries when present.
How to run: Open Command Prompt and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Lists interactive user sessions with session IDs, active or disconnected states, idle times, and logon times.
How to run: Open Command Prompt as administrator and paste this entire file to inspect sessions on the local computer.

Purpose: Deletes the current user's Windows Hello container, including its PIN and associated Hello credentials and keys.
How to run: Open PowerShell as the affected user, paste this entire file, and sign out afterward before setting up Windows Hello again.

Purpose: Displays the Windows Time service synchronization status, time source, and last successful synchronization.
How to run: Open Command Prompt as administrator and paste this entire file on the computer being checked.

Purpose: Installs and imports the Exchange Online PowerShell module, then opens an interactive Exchange Online sign-in.
How to run: Open PowerShell with internet access, paste this entire file, and sign in with an account authorized for the intended tenant.

Purpose: Exports resultant Group Policy for the computer and queried user to an HTML report in the current temporary folder.
How to run: Open Command Prompt as administrator and paste this entire file, then open GPO-Results.html from the temporary folder.

Purpose: Runs verbose domain controller diagnostics and saves the output to C:\Reports\DCDiag_Report.txt.
How to run: Open Command Prompt as administrator on the intended domain controller and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Requests a delta synchronization cycle from the local Microsoft Entra Connect synchronization engine.
How to run: Open Windows PowerShell 5.1 as administrator on the Entra Connect Sync server and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Lists Volume Shadow Copy Service writers and their current state and last reported error.
How to run: Open Command Prompt as administrator and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Displays the serial number reported by the device BIOS.
How to run: Open PowerShell and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Lists physical disk names, reported HDD or SSD media types, sizes, and serial numbers.
How to run: Open PowerShell as administrator and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Displays the manufacturer and model reported by the local computer.
How to run: Open PowerShell and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Displays the health and operational status that Windows reports for each visible physical disk.
How to run: Open PowerShell as administrator and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Displays volume drive letters, labels, reported health, free space, and total capacity in GB.
How to run: Open PowerShell as administrator and paste this entire file on the computer being checked.

Purpose: Uses the reported computer model to estimate whether Windows is running inside a virtual machine.
How to run: Open PowerShell and paste this entire file.

Elevation / effect: Elevation may be requested; test needs restart
Purpose: Opens Windows Memory Diagnostic to schedule a memory test that runs after a restart.
How to run: Press Windows + R and enter only mdsched.exe, or paste this entire file into Command Prompt, then choose the intended restart option.

Purpose: Checks drive C for file-system errors and unreadable sectors while requesting repair and recovery of readable data.
How to run: Paste this file into Command Prompt opened as administrator and accept scheduling only if the required restart is intended.

Purpose: Queries the configured Windows Update source and lists applicable software updates that are not installed.
How to run: Open Windows PowerShell 5.1 as administrator and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Lists installed Windows CBS hotfixes with known installation dates, ordered from newest to oldest.
How to run: Open PowerShell and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Stops Windows Update services, renames the update cache folders for recovery, and starts the services again.
How to run: Open Command Prompt as administrator and run this file one section at a time while checking the service and rename results.

Purpose: Deletes accessible files from the current user's temporary folder and the Windows temporary folder.
How to run: Close applications and paste this file into Command Prompt opened as administrator under the intended user account.

Purpose: Lists the ten processes with the largest current working sets and displays their memory values in MB.
How to run: Open PowerShell and paste this entire file while the memory problem is occurring.

Purpose: Checks and repairs the running Windows component store with DISM, then scans and repairs protected system files with SFC.
How to run: Open Command Prompt as administrator and run each command in order after the previous command finishes.

Purpose: Sends a reboot reminder to the active user session selected from quser output without restarting the computer.
How to run: Open Windows PowerShell 5.1 as administrator, verify the selected quser session ID, and run this file one section at a time.

Purpose: Sets RemoteSigned execution policy for the current PowerShell process only.
How to run: Paste this entire file into the same PowerShell window that will run the intended scripts.

Purpose: Queries an OpenDNS resolver to display the public source IP address that resolver observes.
How to run: Open Command Prompt with DNS access to the OpenDNS resolver and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Displays detailed adapter addressing, gateways, DNS servers, DHCP information, and DNS suffixes.
How to run: Open Command Prompt and paste this entire file on the affected computer.

Purpose: Lists SMB shares hosted by the local computer with their backing paths and descriptions.
How to run: Open PowerShell as administrator on the computer hosting the shares and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Lists listening TCP addresses and ports with the process ID that owns each listener.
How to run: Open PowerShell as administrator and paste this entire file on the computer being investigated.

Purpose: Queries the DNS TXT record at a domain's _dmarc name.
How to run: Replace example.com with the intended domain, then paste this entire file into Command Prompt.

Purpose: Queries the DNS TXT records published at the specified domain name.
How to run: Replace example.com with the intended domain, then paste this entire file into Command Prompt.

Purpose: Tests whether the specified server accepts a TCP connection on port 445 and displays connection diagnostics.
How to run: Replace server01 with the target hostname or IP and adjust the port if needed, then paste this entire file into PowerShell.

Purpose: Generates an HTML battery usage and capacity report and prints the saved report path.
How to run: Open PowerShell in a writable working folder and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Generates an HTML SleepStudy report for supported Modern Standby systems.
How to run: Open PowerShell as administrator in a writable working folder and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Displays the active plan's sleep timeout settings and includes an optional command to disable idle sleep on AC power.
How to run: Paste this file into PowerShell and uncomment the AC timeout command only when disabling idle sleep is intended.

Purpose: Lists available sleep states and contains the PlatformAoAcOverride registry command intended to disable Modern Standby.
How to run: Open PowerShell as administrator, verify device support, and uncomment the registry command only if this workaround and a later restart are intended.

Purpose: Lists machine-wide program names, versions, and publishers from the 64-bit and 32-bit uninstall registry entries.
How to run: Open 64-bit PowerShell on a 64-bit Windows computer and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Starts classic Outlook in safe mode for troubleshooting.
How to run: Press Windows + R and enter only outlook.exe /safe, or paste this entire file into Command Prompt.

Purpose: Opens Print Server Properties on the Drivers tab.
How to run: Press Windows + R and enter only printui.exe /s /t2, or paste this entire file into Command Prompt.

Purpose: Resets the current user's OneDrive sync client using its per-user installation path.
How to run: Press Windows + R and enter only the first command line, or paste this entire file into Command Prompt as the affected user.

Purpose: Stops and relaunches the current user's Windows Explorer shell.
How to run: Paste this entire file into a normal unelevated PowerShell window in the affected user's desktop session.

Purpose: Displays BitLocker encryption, protection, and lock status for the computer's volumes.
How to run: Open Command Prompt as administrator on a device with BitLocker management available and paste this entire file.

Elevation / effect: No for the local certificate inventory
Purpose: Lists expired certificates and certificates expiring within 30 days in the local computer's Personal certificate store.
How to run: Open Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7.1 or newer on Windows and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Displays Microsoft Defender's operating mode, antivirus state, real-time protection state, and last antivirus signature update.
How to run: Open PowerShell as administrator on a device with the Defender module available and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Downloads and silently installs a ScreenConnect client from a supplied installer URL while writing installation logs.
How to run: Save this file as Install-ScreenConnect.ps1 and run it from elevated PowerShell using .\Install-ScreenConnect.ps1 -InstallerUrl 'YOUR_APPROVED_MSI_URL'.

Purpose: Lists scheduled task folders, task names, and current task states.
How to run: Open PowerShell as administrator and paste this entire file to inspect local scheduled tasks.

Purpose: Lists Windows service names, states, startup modes, service accounts, and executable paths.
How to run: Open PowerShell as administrator and paste this entire file on the computer being assessed.

Purpose: Attempts to stop, uninstall, and remove ITSPlatform components that match the configured names and installation paths.
How to run: Verify the exact installed component names and uninstall strings, save this file as Remove-ITSPlatform.ps1, then run it with elevated Windows PowerShell.

Purpose: Updates Microsoft Defender antimalware signatures and displays their last update time and version.
How to run: Open PowerShell as administrator on a device using Microsoft Defender Antivirus and paste this entire file.

Purpose: Invokes the Windows product-key change tool with the generic Pro edition key without upgrading Windows 10 to Windows 11 or supplying a Pro license.
How to run: Verify the supported edition-change method and a valid Pro license, then paste this file into Command Prompt opened as administrator.

Purpose: Invokes the OOBE network-requirement bypass script if it is available on the installed Windows build.
How to run: During Windows setup, press Shift + F10 to open Command Prompt and paste this file only if the bypass script is available and the restart is intended.
